To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the simplification technique is an efficient way to reduce the number of bus accesses required for a global communication, (2) simplification can be used in order to reduce the number bus accesses required for global communications in hypergrid and hyperpath architectures, (3) hypergrid and hyperpaths can be used to efficiently implement all-to-all communications, (4) the hyperpath architecture is better than the hypergrid architecture for global communication.

(1) The hyperpath and the grid architectures can be simplified to the linear and the hypercube architectures, respectively, without any loss in communication efficiency; (2) The simplification of hyperpaths is more efficient than that of grids; (3) For the simplification of hypergrids, the hyperpath architecture is more efficient than the grid; and (4) The simplification process is more efficient than any other known gossiping algorithm for these architectures.
the hypergrid and the hyperpath architectures can achieve a communication efficiency that is very close to the theoretical optimum for the corresponding point-to-point architectures.
